correctness.rationale: For a finite simplicial complex L whose nonempty faces cover its r vertices, select distinct primes p_i and an auxiliary larger q and set N=q product p_i. The symmetric Cayley digraph with steps ±1, ±d_F (d_F product of primes in facet F) is strongly connected and satisfies Hultman 2-density due to reverse arcs. Geometric cyclic fixed points have barycentric weights constant on each full arc orbit; their supports are unions of orbits, yielding the actual orbit-barycenter simplicial model, not just fixed vertices. A union of step orbits is non-strongly connected precisely when gcd(N,step set)>1, because a finite cyclic semigroup is its generated subgroup. Since q divides no d_F, the remaining complex is the union of full simplices on orbit steps divisible by each p_i. Every nonempty multiple intersection is a simplex, and the nerve has exactly the faces of L. Nerve lemma thus proves fixed space homotopy ≃|L|. Hultman 2004 theorem supplies ambient wedge spheres dimension 2N-4 for strongly connected 2-dense digraph; chromatic coefficient nonzero for connected underlying graph. Independent complete arithmetic subset test for L=boundary triangle, N=210 and eight steps checked all 256 subsets against gcd/prime-cover criterion. Source verifier was read: its five finite nerve/homology cases corroborate only small examples.
